title: Artin acyclicity for intersections of projective strict localizations
statement:
Let $B$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:P\to B$ be a projective morphism [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Let $x,u$ be any two geometric points of $P$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and form their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$W=P_{(x)}\times_P P_{(u)}.$$
For every torsion abelian sheaf $A$ on the small etale site of $W$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf],
$$H^i(W_{\mathrm{Et}},A)=0\quad\text{for all }i>0,$$
where cohomology is derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The fibre product may be empty or have infinitely many connected components. No Noetherian hypothesis on $B$, constructibility hypothesis on $A$, or invertibility of its torsion orders is imposed.

source.place: Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme, Theorem 7.10 (etale case), Definition 7.8 and Proposition 7.9, printed pp. 14–15; read online, local copy WANTED. Common-affine specialization for projective P: Orgogozo, Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4.
